promise: Hassabis predicted that artificial general intelligence could emerge in roughly five to ten years.
description: Hassabis gave an approximate forecast for AGI at a March 2025 briefing. It is not a fixed end-of-2035 delivery commitment.
evidence: CNBC's summary reports a five-to-ten-year expectation, not an unconditional deadline.

review.note: This is an approximate five-to-ten-year forecast, not a guarantee that every task will be solved by December 2035. The source points to a March 17 briefing; the exact original article should be checked before converting the window to a precise daily deadline. Unsupported 2026 revisions are removed.

promise: Reduce the net carbon intensity of our energy products by 20% by 2030 and 45% by 2035, versus 2016 (net zero by 2050).
description: Shell retired its 45% net-carbon-intensity reduction target for 2035 on 14 March 2024 and revised its 2030 target from 20% to 15-20%, relative to 2016.
evidence: Shell's 2024 strategy explicitly retires the 2035 intensity target and revises the 2030 range.

review.note: The rollback occurred on 14 March 2024, not 14 June 2023. The revised 2030 intensity range was 15-20%, not 9-12% (the latter was a 2024 target). The 2035 target was retired. Exact 2021 announcement day and ancillary court claim not established; remove superlative.

promise: Invest 5% of GDP annually in defence by 2035, including at least 3.5% on core defence and up to 1.5% on related security spending
description: At The Hague summit on June 25, 2025, NATO allies adopted the 2035 investment commitment. The target distinguishes core military expenditure from broader defence- and security-related investment.
evidence: NATO's official account confirms the target and 2035 horizon; final fulfillment is not yet due.

role: Parties to the UNFCCC Paris Agreement
promise: Provide at least $300 billion per year in climate finance to developing countries by 2035, with $1.3 trillion as the overall ambition
description: COP29 adopted the new finance goal early November 24 in Baku, still November 23 UTC: at least $300 billion annually by 2035 with developed countries taking the lead, alongside efforts to scale all-source finance to $1.3 trillion annually.
evidence: UNFCCC confirms the finance targets; their 2035 implementation horizon remains ahead.

promise: Canada will meet NATO's new Defence Investment Pledge of 5% of GDP by 2035, and double defence expenditures with an additional C$80 billion over five years
description: Canada joined the June 25, 2025 NATO commitment to 5% of GDP in core defence and related security investment by 2035. In February 2026 the PMO reaffirmed the target and described reaching 2% in fiscal 2025-26.
evidence: Canada joined the new NATO Defence Investment Pledge on June 25, 2025
Carney reaffirmed doubling defence spending and the 5% by 2035 target in February 2026

review.note: 5% target is supported. February source specifies 2% in fiscal 2025-26, not calendar2026, and discusses distinct ten-year procurement/capital totals. The additional $80bn/five-year doubling claim is not established as part of the June 2025 commitment.

promise: Achieve carbon neutrality across the entire battery value chain by 2035, with supplier carbon-footprint data required from 2027
description: CATL reiterated its 2035 value-chain carbon-neutrality goal in Ningde on August 17, 2026 and announced supplier carbon-footprint reporting requirements from 2027. It said all 20 battery plants had received carbon-neutral certification for its core-operations target.
evidence: CATL's August 17 release supports the roadmap and reporting requirement; core-operation certification does not establish value-chain neutrality.
